payload.title: What Are the Brazilian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Brazilian wedding traditions in the order they tend to happen, from the noivado to the sweets handed out as guests leave, plus what Australian couples should know about marrying legally in Brazil.
key_takeaways: It is often told that couples wear the aliança on the right hand while engaged and move it to the left hand during the wedding.
Padrinhos and madrinhas are formal witnesses to the wedding, so choose them for the role and not only for the photographs.

Lighter customs that are often told include Santo Antônio's June festivities, unmarried friends' names written inside the bride's hem, the groom's tie cut into keepsakes and bem-casados handed to guests as they leave.
Australians marrying in Brazil should confirm documents with the cartório first, then book any notarial appointment in Brasília or São Paulo, not Rio de Janeiro.

faq.q: What finger do Brazilians wear their wedding ring on?
faq.a: It is often told that Brazilian couples wear the aliança on the right ring finger during the engagement and move it to the left ring finger at the wedding. The aliança itself is a ring that symbolises engagement or marriage. Practice varies by family.

faq.q: What happens if I marry a Brazilian in Brazil?
faq.a: A civil marriage goes through the cartório de registro civil and a process called habilitação, so confirm the steps, documents and fees with the cartório and the Australian Embassy in Brasília. The Embassy will not advise which documents Brazil needs, so ask the cartório first. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
faq.a: There is no single figure. Ask the cartório directly about its fees, and note that a fee applies to an Australian CNI and to notarial services. Celebration costs depend on the place, the season and the guest list, so ask for every quote and its inclusions in writing.

faq.q: What are bem-casados and why are they given at weddings?
faq.a: A bem-casado is a small, soft sponge cake made of two halves. It is often told that the joined halves stand for the couple and that eating one wishes them a good marriage, which is why many couples give them to guests as they leave.

faq.q: What do guests wear to a Brazilian wedding?
faq.a: Follow the dress code on the invitation, and ask the couple if it is unclear. For a wedding in Brazil, check the season and region on Smartraveller too, since the wet season falls at different times in the north, north-east and south.

faq.q: Who are padrinhos and madrinhas at a Brazilian wedding?
faq.a: They are the couple's wedding sponsors and witnesses: the Priberam dictionary defines a madrinha as a woman who serves as a witness at a baptism or wedding. It is often told that couples choose several pairs from both families.
